verdict.rationale: Letta scopes memory at the agent level: each agent has its own identity and long-term memory, and cross-agent sharing happens only through explicitly created shared-memory repositories. At the organization level, teammates' agents and conversations are private by default, with roles and sharing controls governing access. Memory is not documented as being partitioned by end user or by application inside one deployment, so tenant isolation in practice means one agent per tenant. Missing for 10: documented per-end-user and per-application memory scoping, explicit guarantees that retrieval and search never cross tenant boundaries, and independent or hands-on corroboration of isolation.
